lc_person: Amy Kaplan, University of Pennsylvania professor of English and scholar of American literature and imperialism; author of The Social Construction of American Realism and co-editor of Cultures of United States Imperialism.
item_person: Amy Kaplan (1953–2020), academic and American studies scholar, identified by LC n87888028 and VIAF 56706519.

evidence.says: LC names Kaplan, Amy and cites The Social Construction of American Realism (1988) and Cultures of United States Imperialism (1993). The latter CIP data sheet supplies birth year 1943. LC also cites her Penn faculty page and obituary, identifying the same English professor, scholarly field and books, and reporting death in 2020 at age 66.

Q98066322 is labeled Amy Kaplan, described as an academic, and records birth year 1953, death year 2020, LC authority n87888028 (P244), and VIAF 56706519. Its English Wikipedia sitelink is Amy Kaplan.

Penn identifies Amy Kaplan as its English professor and a scholar of American literary and cultural studies. It lists The Social Construction of American Realism (1988), Cultures of U.S. Imperialism (1993), The Anarchy of Empire (2002), and Our American Israel (2018), and reports that she died in 2020 at age 66.

Melani McAlister’s memorial in Passport, January 2021, pp. 65–67, explicitly gives Amy Kaplan’s years as 1953–2020 and identifies the Penn English professor, former American Studies Association president, and scholar of U.S. culture and empire.

notes: Matching authority identifier, name, works and institutional biography establish the same person despite the birth discrepancy. The scholarly memorial supports 1953; LC’s 1943 appears erroneous. The graph’s supplied key evidence is only the citation name kaplan|amy, which is consistent with this scholar but supplies no independent biographical detail.
